title: Episode 00 — We built the newsroom first
_production: THE BONES OF THE EPISODE. Render this, drop it into Detail or Captions on
the phone, and film yourself into the five `question` scenes. Each one
prints a dim [ your answer, ~Ns ] cue telling you how long you have.
EVERY CLAIM BELOW IS CHECKABLE AGAINST THIS REPOSITORY. Nothing here
characterizes anyone or asserts anything about a person. That is on
purpose: episode 00 is about the method, so the method is the only
subject. Numbers are re-verified by running `bin/sentinel test`.
Photos are deliberately absent. See ../../docs/SHOTLIST.md — episode 01
is where the world comes in.

scenes.title: We built the newsroom first.
scenes.sub: Before the first story, the machine that has to survive being wrong.
scenes.vo: Most people start with the story. We started with what makes it trustworthy.
scenes.delivery: Flat. No lift at the end. This is a statement, not a pitch.
scenes.source_note: Framing only. No claim about any person.

scenes.question: Why build the tools before the story?

scenes.caption: things this system refuses to do.
scenes.sub: Each one blocked by a database constraint, a trigger, or a code path — not by remembering to be careful at 2 a.m.
scenes.vo: Nine refusals. Not policies. Constraints in the database that stop the thing happening.
scenes.delivery: Slow on the number. Let it sit before the caption lands.
scenes.source_note: Count of data rows in the 'What it refuses to do' table in README.md.

scenes.label: THE RULE
scenes.source: Source: README.md — "The two rules everything else follows"
scenes.vo: Holding a document and its hash means you have it. It does not mean anyone has read it.
scenes.delivery: This is the thesis. Slower than everything around it.
scenes.source_note: GREEN — verbatim from README.md in this repository.

scenes.question: What stops you publishing something you can't prove?

scenes.kick: THE RENDERER THAT MADE THIS VIDEO
scenes.caption: checks run before a frame is drawn.
scenes.sub: Unknown scene type, missing field, missing asset, a hash that does not match its file — each one fails the build instead of shipping.
scenes.vo: The engine that made this video checks itself first. It refuses frames it cannot verify.
scenes.delivery: Matter-of-fact. This is a spec sheet, not a boast.
scenes.source_note: Printed by `openmontage.py --self-test`. This number moves whenever the engine gains a check — re-run it and update this field before publishing.

scenes.title: Documents and dates. No characterization.
scenes.sub: The record, stated flatly, is harder to argue with than any adjective — and it cannot be used against you later.
scenes.vo: Facts with citations. No characterization. A flat timeline survives a deposition. An adjective does not.
scenes.delivery: Hard cut in. Say it once, plainly, and stop.
scenes.source_note: The writing rule this newsroom holds itself to.

scenes.question: So what is the first story?
scenes.source_note: Host scene. Film yourself here. This is the hook into episode 01.

scenes.title: Every build carries a receipt.
scenes.sub: Spec, data, images and output — all hashed into a manifest beside the video.
scenes.cta: If the video claims it, the build enforces it.
scenes.vo: Every render writes a manifest. The spec, every file it read, the video itself. Anyone can check.
scenes.delivery: Close it out. Land on the last line and let the hash finish typing.
scenes.source_note: GREEN — the hash is verified against a real file at build time. A mismatch refuses the render.
